title: Untitled project folder names can carry C0/C1 into board spans
description: On Unix a directory name may contain a C0 or C1 character. If the operator opens that directory as a Git project and the project has no title, ProjectNames::name returns the raw folder name. The wide task-column header state places that name in a Span. A project group header does the same. When the line fits, bound_line returns the spans unchanged, so terminal_text never runs, and put_line renders them on the next draw_board, including after ctrl+l. Whether ratatui then writes the scalar to the tty as a control is outside this crate and was not observed.
claimed_root_cause: An untitled project's folder name is copied into the task-header state and the project group header, and bound_line keeps a fitting line, so those spans skip terminal_text.

trace.description: A Git root becomes the project scope path through to_string_lossy, which keeps valid C0 and C1 scalars from the directory name.
A capture with no scope override stores snapshot.default_scope on the new task, so the directory path becomes task.scope.
With no project title, name returns project_basename of that path, the last component, with no control-character filter.
project_name returns ProjectNames::name of the path string and does not call terminal_text.
For a project task, the header state is the status word plus project_name, so the raw folder name is part of header.state.
The state string is placed in Span::styled. The title beside it goes through present_line; the state span does not.
When line.width() is within max_width, bound_line returns the original line. present_line runs only after that check fails.
A fitting line is padded and frame.render_widget paints the Paragraph. The original spans, including the folder name, are still in that line.

evidence.description: project_basename is the last non-empty path component and does not inspect control characters.
group_key's project label is names.name(path), the same untitled folder name.
paint_group_header puts that label in Span::styled(word) and then calls bound_line, with no terminal_text on the word.
A group-header row is drawn with put_line, so a fitting group label reaches the same renderer as the task-header state.
terminal_text rewrites every char::is_control scalar, which covers C0 and C1, but the header-state and group-word spans do not call it.
project_option_label does wrap the folder name in terminal_text. task_header_state and group_key use ProjectNames::name instead.
project_title_refusal rejects a control character only for a title passed through the setter. An untitled project never takes that path.
Unix mode 0600 is applied to store files created here. It does not constrain directory names on disk.
A comment on the Unix-only setup listing test says Win32 rejects control characters such as ESC in directory names. The test at line 1615 creates a directory whose name contains U+001B.
ctrl+l is consumed by redraw_on_request, and the loop continues into the next draw_board paint.

blockers: Cargo and the tsk binary were not run, and the cargo registry is absent, so ratatui was not executed and no TestBackend or tty capture shows the bytes written for a Span that contains a C0 or C1 scalar.
Ratatui's buffer and backend sources are not in this workspace, so whether a zero-width control stored in a cell symbol is emitted to the tty or dropped cannot be read here.

validation_plan.local: With a local toolchain, render draw_board into a ratatui TestBackend for an untitled project whose folder name contains U+001B, with one task in that project and a frame wide enough that the header state fits. Assert the state cell symbol still contains U+001B. Repeat with grouping set to project and assert the group-header word cell. A second local backend that records its write can show whether that symbol is emitted as the ESC byte. Keep the check on a local TestBackend.

title: Windows state files inherit the parent directory DACL
description: Windows state files and directories are created with no security descriptor. default_state_dir selects LOCALAPPDATA\tsk, or USERPROFILE\.tsk when LOCALAPPDATA is empty. ensure_private_dir creates that directory with create_dir_all and tightens it to 0700 only on Unix. Saves write tsk.json through create_private_file, which sets mode 0600 only on Unix and otherwise uses OpenOptions with no SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES. tighten_file, which save runs over existing state names, is a no-op off Unix. Lock files use the same Unix-only mode. On non-Unix, write_launcher creates launchers with create_dir_all and fs::write. config.toml temps from create_private_temp do the same. install.ps1 creates the binary directory LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\tsk\bin, or TSK_INSTALL_DIR, with New-Item. It does not Set-Acl and does not create the state directory. No source file assigns a Windows DACL, so each new object inherits its parent directory DACL. That DACL is not in the repository.
claimed_root_cause: State directories and files are created with std::fs::create_dir_all, OpenOptions::open, and std::fs::write and no Windows security descriptor. Owner-only mode and tighten_file are compiled only for Unix, so each new Windows object inherits its parent directory DACL. This repository neither writes nor reads that DACL.

trace.description: On Windows the state directory is LOCALAPPDATA\tsk when LOCALAPPDATA is non-empty, otherwise USERPROFILE\.tsk, otherwise a relative .tsk-state. The function returns a path and does not create it or attach a security descriptor.
A missing directory is created with fs::create_dir_all. The only permission change, tighten_private_dir, is cfg(unix) at line 55. The Windows path passes no SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES.

After ensure_private_dir at line 829, the save creates the temp document that is replaced onto tsk.json through AtomicFilesystem::create_file. StdFilesystem::create_file at line 325 delegates to create_private_file.

The file is opened write/create/truncate. mode 0600 is applied only inside cfg(unix) at lines 176-179. The Windows open supplies no security descriptor, so a new file inherits the parent directory DACL.

The non-Unix branch creates the launchers directory with create_dir_all and writes the PowerShell script with fs::write. launcher_file at line 1143 places that script under the state directory. Neither call sets a DACL. powershell_script only builds the script text.
config.toml temps are create_new OpenOptions. mode 0600 is cfg(unix) only at lines 284-288, and options.open at line 289 sets no Windows security descriptor.

Off Unix the helper ignores the path. Save, lock open, and restore call it for existing state files, and it never assigns a Windows security descriptor. The directory, tsk.json, lock, config temp, and launcher keep the inherited parent DACL.

evidence.description: The module states that no permission is claimed on non-Unix platforms and that the helpers compile down to plain create or copy.
create_private_file ends in options.open with no Windows security attributes.
open_lock_file sets mode 0600 only inside cfg(unix) in lock_open_options. The Windows lock create has no security descriptor.
The primary Windows state path is LOCALAPPDATA joined with tsk.
tighten_state_files runs before the new document is written, and on Windows tighten_file does not change a DACL.
A Windows launch writes launcher bytes from powershell_script through write_launcher. The script text does not set an ACL.
The default install directory is LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\tsk\bin, or TSK_INSTALL_DIR. That is the binary directory, not the state directory.
The installer creates the install directory with New-Item. The script contains no Set-Acl, Get-Acl, or icacls call.
windows-sys enables the Win32_Security feature, but no Rust source imports Win32::Security or calls a DACL or security-descriptor API.

blockers: The inherited DACL is an operating-system fact. This repository never sets a Windows security descriptor, so source cannot show whether a second non-admin account has an allow ACE on the state directory, tsk.json, or a launcher script.
This host is Linux, so the DACL was not observed and target code was not executed.

validation_plan.local: On a fresh non-admin Windows profile, run tsk add with a dummy title and record icacls of the new state directory and tsk.json without changing the ACL.
validation_plan.deployment: On an existing store, record icacls of the state directory, tsk.json, and any launcher script without changing the ACL or opening the files.
